commands.review_summary:
Adds a workflow utility and apply status text that bucket selected close candidates by quality, plus scheduler documentation and focused workflow utility tests.

Reproducibility: yes. Source inspection shows the new summary block runs before reconcile while the real apply selection still runs after reconcile, so a stale or reopened record changed by reconcile reproduces the mismatch path.
commands.review_followup: - [P2] A narrow automated repair can move the summary generation after reconcile, add a workflow-ordering regression check, and leave the rest of the feature intact.

target.title: feat: summarize close candidate quality
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Apply can have a valid queue of close candidates, but maintainers only see a flat list/count. That makes very different situations look the same: straightforward implemented-on-main closes, PR duplicate closes that still need coverage proof, policy-sensitive candidates, stale/low-signal cleanup, and candidates that are only retrying after an earlier guard skip.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Adds `proposed-item-quality-summary`, a reporting-only workflow utility that reuses the same close-candidate selector as `proposed-item-numbers`.
- Groups selected candidates into operator-facing buckets: implemented-on-main, duplicate/superseded, needs PR close proof, aging/low-signal, policy-sensitive, retry after guard skip, and other.
- Adds the summary to apply status detail as `Close candidate mix: ...` for close-mode runs.
- Keeps the dashboard quiet: this only enriches existing apply status text and does not create a new alert/card.
- Documents that the buckets are telemetry only and do not change candidate eligibility, limits, live-state checks, or policy gates.

## User Impact

Maintainers can quickly tell what kind of pruning work the apply lane is about to attempt. The status stays concise and action-oriented, for example:

```text
Close candidate mix: 1 implemented-on-main, 1 needs PR close proof, 1 aging/low-signal
```

## Evidence

Focused local proof:

```powershell
pnpm run format
pnpm run build:all
node --test test\repair\workflow-utils.test.ts test\sweep-workflow.test.ts
pnpm run format:check
```

Result: passed. The focused test run reported 64 tests, 63 passing, 1 skipped.

Direct CLI proof from a temporary records tree:

```text
candidate_quality_total=3
candidate_quality_summary=1 implemented-on-main, 1 needs PR close proof, 1 aging/low-signal
candidate_quality_buckets_json=[{"bucket":"ready_implemented","count":1,"label":"implemented-on-main","next_step":"Live-state checks can close these if the item is still unchanged."},{"bucket":"needs_pr_close_coverage","count":1,"label":"needs PR close proof","next_step":"Run or reuse close-coverage proof before closing the PR."},{"bucket":"aging_or_low_signal","count":1,"label":"aging/low-signal","next_step":"Rely on stale-age and live-state checks; inspect if this bucket dominates."}]
```

Full local check:

```powershell
$env:PNPM_BIN='C:\Users\marti\AppData\Local\Corepack\shims\pnpm.cmd'
pnpm run check
```

Result: passed. The full check reported 1147 tests, 1146 passing, 1 skipped, coverage gates at 100%, and format clean.

Codex review:

```powershell
codex review -c service_tier='fast' --base origin/main
```

Result: no actionable correctness issues found. The review noted the telemetry is consistent with the existing candidate-selection path.

## Screenshots / Visual Proof

No new dashboard surface is added. The visible operator surface is the apply status detail text shown above.

## Dependency / Stack Note

This is based on current main after #391, #397, and #395. It is conceptually independent from #398 and #401, but it touches the same apply workflow/status area; if #398 or #401 lands first, this branch should be rebased to preserve all status text.

## Risk Notes

- Reporting only: no new close/comment/label/merge behavior.
- Uses the existing candidate selector so the bucket counts cannot include records that apply would not consider.
- Does not change close limits, cursor behavior, live-state checks, policy gates, or permissions.
